purpose: Distinct real-world twin and shadow families connect to Q Pueblo subjects as bounded contextual and learning inputs, not as autonomous authorities or an assertion that a live digital twin exists.

twinTypes.title: Physical infrastructure
twinTypes.description: Assets, capacity, failures, repairs and lifecycle

twinTypes.title: Water and energy networks
twinTypes.description: Reservoir, supply, grid, fuel and dependency behavior

twinTypes.title: Services and operations
twinTypes.description: Process steps, workforce capacity and service continuity

twinTypes.title: Government and institutional authority
twinTypes.description: Dated roles, jurisdiction, decision paths and oversight

twinTypes.title: Public and regional finance
twinTypes.description: Budgets, awards, contracts, payments, outcomes and debt

twinTypes.title: Population health and service capacity
twinTypes.description: Aggregate care access and public-health system loads, never diagnoses

twinTypes.title: School and learning systems
twinTypes.description: Enrollment, facilities, programs, access and measurable outcomes

twinTypes.title: Housing and community resources
twinTypes.description: Aggregate housing supply, affordability and community service coverage

twinTypes.title: Food and agricultural systems
twinTypes.description: Crops, irrigation, storage, food supply and producer dependencies

twinTypes.title: Ecosystems and natural resources
twinTypes.description: Water, land, air, habitat, drought, wildfire and restoration

twinTypes.title: Mobility and logistics
twinTypes.description: Roads, bridges, freight, rail, airport, transit and access

twinTypes.title: Digital systems and cyber resilience
twinTypes.description: Networks, service dependencies, integrity and safe failure

twinTypes.title: Jobs and supply chains
twinTypes.description: Regional employment, employers, labor and essential inputs

twinTypes.title: Historical and future systems
twinTypes.description: Observed past states, scenario branches and uncertain future alternatives

shadowTypes.title: Observation shadow
shadowTypes.description: Read-only view of publicly sourced conditions, not direct control

shadowTypes.title: Baseline and comparator shadow
shadowTypes.description: Compare before/after records, institutional alternatives or human-reviewed baselines

shadowTypes.title: Counterfactual shadow
shadowTypes.description: What-if comparison using explicit assumptions, not an observed outcome

shadowTypes.title: Failure and cascading-risk shadow
shadowTypes.description: Explore SHOCK dependencies and independent backup failures as scenarios

shadowTypes.title: Adversarial testing shadow
shadowTypes.description: Bounded defensive test results without offensive execution or live intrusion

shadowTypes.title: Evidence-quality shadow
shadowTypes.description: Source ages, contradictions, missing coverage and provenance problems

shadowTypes.title: Policy and authority shadow
shadowTypes.description: Compare proposed versus effective rules and documented accountable authorities

shadowTypes.title: Financial shadow
shadowTypes.description: Reconcile proposed, awarded, invoiced, paid and delivered spending

shadowTypes.title: Environmental shadow
shadowTypes.description: Track source-verified changes in ecological conditions without claiming full causal proof

shadowTypes.title: Community-impact shadow
shadowTypes.description: Aggregate service and access outcomes, not profiles of individual residents

shadowTypes.title: External model shadow
shadowTypes.description: Compare licensed model output with observed records and independent benchmarks

shadowTypes.title: Historical-version shadow
shadowTypes.description: Maintain past snapshots and correction lineage without retroactive erasure

shadowTypes.title: Human functional shadow
shadowTypes.description: Private, consent-bound personal-support concept, never a public person replica
